hero.label: Made for Revise Robotics
hero.headline: I want to help Revise put more refurbished laptops in more hands.
hero.subheadline: Revise Robotics is attacking a $1T market while keeping electronics out of shredders and into the hands of people who actually need them. Antonio's story about his cousin refurbishing laptops in Mexico hit close to home for me as a Spanish speaker who has seen firsthand how much a working device can change someone's trajectory. I want to be the person helping Revise find the supply to make that mission scale.

whyCompany.title: Robotic refurbishment solves the supply bottleneck nobody else is automating
whyCompany.body: Most refurbishers are still doing this manually, which caps how many devices they can process. Revise is using industrial automation and AI to test, repair, and verify at a speed no human team can match. That is not an incremental improvement, that is a category-defining wedge into a market that has barely started to be touched.

whyCompany.title: Three employees, two open roles, and YC behind it
whyCompany.body: Revise was founded in 2024, has three people on the team, and is already hiring for both sales and engineering. That means the business development work I would do this summer would not be one small piece of a large org chart. It would be foundational, with real weight, and I would be building alongside Rupesh and Antonio from nearly the beginning.

whyCompany.title: Cold outreach and pipeline building are exactly what I have been doing
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach campaigns through HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences that helped acquire 15 to 20 paying clients from scratch. At NextAfter I sharpened that in a B2B environment where messaging precision actually moved numbers. Finding and closing laptop procurement partners for Revise is the same muscle, just pointed at a problem I find genuinely exciting.

quote: Antonio's cousin was refurbishing laptops by hand in Mexico long before any robot could help him. I grew up around that same resourcefulness, and I want to spend my summer making sure Revise never runs out of devices to fix.
